question: What can a fixed prerequisite architecture alone imply about which concepts a learner can understand, the rate at which target information becomes usable, finite-horizon teaching thresholds, resource allocation, and the cost of one curriculum for heterogeneous learners?

key_findings.claim: A mind's finitary prerequisite rules generate an algebraic closure operator, and its understanding horizon is the least rule-closed superset of its axioms.
key_findings.evidence: The one-step expansion operator repeatedly adds every concept whose finite prerequisite set is present. Proposition 2.10 identifies the least fixed point with the union of finite iterates, Proposition 2.11 characterizes the horizon axiomatically, and the derivation theorem makes membership equivalent to a finite proof tree. This is a formal reachability notion, not semantic comprehension or truth.

key_findings.claim: Under a finite understanding horizon, the prerequisite-respecting acquired states form an axiom-based learning space, and conversely every such learning space can be represented by expansion rules.
key_findings.evidence: Reachability is defined operationally by adjoining one currently ordered concept at a time. Proposition 2.24 proves accessibility and union closure; Corollary 2.26 identifies the shifted antimatroid; Theorem 2.27 supplies the converse representation. The finiteness assumption is doing material work: these statements do not cover infinite state families or cognitive operations that remove, revise, or jointly acquire concepts.

key_findings.claim: The stochastic teaching channel is state gated: one raw signal is either passed unchanged or collapsed to a single null symbol, and only a passed signal can add its target concept.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 3.3's memoryless sharp parser returns z when tgt(z) is currently ordered and bottom otherwise. The update rule adds at most one parsed target per round and does not buffer an earlier unparseable signal for later use. Thus all structural lower bounds partly encode the selected parser and one-concept-per-round convention, rather than following from prerequisites alone.

key_findings.claim: Usable information is correctly treated as relative to learner state, but the null symbol is not generally equivalent to target-independent noise.
key_findings.evidence: The posterior entropy drop is conditional mutual information, and Section 3.3 distinguishes two separate phenomena: an eventwise erasure can still be informative because observing bottom reveals which target-conditioned signal was unparseable, while a perfectly parseable signal may be independent of the target and convey zero information. The paper's informal language that unparseable information is noise therefore needs this conditional qualification.

key_findings.claim: Larger acquired states weakly increase parsed output entropy and Blackwell-dominate smaller states on every realized public history, although the paper's 'capacity' is only output-alphabet cardinality under the sharp parser.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 4.2 takes a supremum over the entropy of rho_m(Z,K), not mutual information for a fixed target-to-signal channel. Lemma A.5 computes it exactly as log(|Z_ord(K)|+1) when any signal is erased and log|Z| otherwise. Lemma 4.4 makes this quantity monotone, and Theorem 4.6 constructs the smaller-state observation as a deterministic garbling of the larger-state observation. These are exact combinatorial and decision-theoretic statements conditional on the fixed parser and next-signal law, not an optimized Shannon channel capacity or empirical claim about neural decoding.

anchors.section: Appendix A.3 / proofs of Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.6

key_findings.claim: The advertised structural-information speed law is valid, but the epistemic term is provably at most one round in the paper's own baseline model.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.11 gives E[tau] at least the maximum of expected structural distance and H(Theta)/Cmax. Proposition 4.13 then observes that distinct direct target signals make H(Theta)/Cmax no greater than 1; with signals available for every prerequisite, a curriculum completes within L_m(Theta)+1. Consequently the structural term normally dominates, so the abstract's presentation of two substantial speed limits overstates what the baseline instantiation can demonstrate.

key_findings.claim: Mathematical boundary audit: the central ratio H(Theta)/C_m^max is undefined in an allowed deterministic one-signal instance, because both numerator and denominator can be zero.
key_findings.evidence: The setup permits a singleton target set and requires only one raw signal for that target. If Z contains exactly that signal, the parsed range has cardinality one at every state, so Lemma A.5 gives C_m^max=log 1=0, while a deterministic target has H(Theta)=0. Theorem 4.11 and Proposition 4.13(i) nevertheless write 0/0 and make no positivity assumption or convention. Their proofs establish the division-free inequality H(Theta)<=C_m^max; the ratio form is valid only when C_m^max>0, with the zero-capacity deterministic case handled separately.

anchors.section: Appendix A.3 / proofs of Theorem 4.11 and Proposition 4.13

key_findings.claim: A worked four-target chain confirms that structural preparation can be necessary before target-specific signaling, while also illustrating why the information lower bound is nonbinding.
key_findings.evidence: In Example 4.14 all four targets share prerequisite b. An immediate target signal produces bottom with probability one and zero mutual information; teaching b first opens a parseable alphabet, after which one target-specific signal completes teaching. The achieved two rounds equal structural depth 2, whereas H/Cmax is only 2/log 5 and the general direct-signaling bound is at most one.

key_findings.claim: The exact zero-to-one completion threshold holds only for a deterministic target; random targets receive only a depth-distribution upper bound and eventual-success statement.
key_findings.evidence: For general Theta, Proposition 5.1 says V(t) is at most P[L_m(Theta) <= t] and is zero only below the minimum supported depth; Proposition 5.2 gives convergence to one when some strategy has finite mean completion time. Proposition 5.3 becomes an exact step at L_m(g) only after making the prior degenerate, so the broad language that completion probability jumps at one prerequisite depth should not be transferred to heterogeneous random targets.

key_findings.claim: Concentrating a scarce training budget beats spreading it only in a deliberately thresholded, identical-learner, deterministic-target objective.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 5.5 gives zero completed learners when everyone receives fewer than L rounds and constructs an allocation completing min(N,floor(B/L)) learners by giving each selected learner exactly L. It does not compare fairness, partial competence, heterogeneous depths, uncertainty, opportunity costs, or concave benefits below completion, so it is a mathematical corner result rather than a general policy recommendation.

key_findings.claim: A universal broadcast can be a factor linear in learner types slower than personalized curricula, but the theorem is an extremal existence construction rather than a universal lower bound.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 5.6 builds k minds with disjoint private prerequisite chains of personalized length L. Any common sequence teaching their shared target needs exactly k(L-1)+1 signals because each chain must be paid separately. The proof explicitly engineers non-reusable prerequisites; it does not say typical classrooms, partially aligned minds, adaptive group instruction, or feedback must incur that penalty.

key_findings.claim: The paper contains no empirical, computational, or human-subject evaluation of whether the formal states, parser, or predicted thresholds describe real learning.
key_findings.evidence: All reported evidence consists of definitions, formal propositions, proofs, and hand-constructed examples. There are no datasets, learners, measured outcomes, simulations, uncertainty intervals, empirical baselines, or falsification tests; the 51-page document devotes pages 35-49 to proofs and pages 50-51 to references.

anchors.section: 5.2 / final theorem and end of main text

method.core_idea: Model understanding as reachability in a prerequisite-rule closure system, then treat teaching as sequential communication through a learner-state-dependent erasure channel whose decoder expands one acquired concept at a time.
method.mechanism: A mind m=(C,A_m,E_m) defines a monotone one-step operator Phi_m and closure cl_m; its horizon U_m is cl_m(A_m). Ordered concepts are those enabled at the current acquired set. A sharp parser exposes only signals whose target is ordered and replaces all others with bottom. A teacher who observes the latent target chooses signals; the learner updates a Bayesian posterior over a finite target set and adds at most one parsed concept. Structural distance is shortest prerequisite-respecting acquisition length, while state-dependent parsed entropy gives an information budget. These components yield lower and upper completion-time bounds, fixed-horizon threshold results, an allocation corollary, and a constructed separation between personalized and broadcast sequences.
assumptions: The concept set is discrete, prerequisite sets are finite, and the main learning-space and stochastic results use a finite understanding horizon or finite target support.
A learner's axioms and prerequisite rules are fixed during teaching; development that changes the rule architecture is treated as a different mind.
Rules encode only positive reachability: there is no inconsistency, truth status, belief revision, forgetting, interference, or removal of an acquired concept.
A concept is acquired atomically and at most one concept can be added per instructional round.
The sharp parser is deterministic and memoryless; an unparseable signal is collapsed to one bottom symbol and is never buffered for later reinterpretation.
Every target has a distinct raw signal, and the constructive upper bounds further assume a signal exists for every intermediate prerequisite.
The ratio form of the epistemic lower bound implicitly requires C_m^max>0, although the written setup allows a deterministic one-signal case with H(Theta)=C_m^max=0.
The teacher knows the realized target and enough of the learner architecture to select a valid ordered curriculum.
The learner's posterior is the exact Bayesian conditional distribution under a common prior and common knowledge of the strategy and parser.
Completion requires both physical acquisition of the realized target and exact posterior identification with mass one.
Round count treats every signal and every concept as equally costly and ignores response latency, practice, transfer, and parallel acquisition.
Multi-learner broadcast is a single open-loop raw-signal sequence; personalization may use each mind's private chain without a shared cost model.
Economic output in the allocation result counts only fully completed learners and assigns no value to partial learning or distributive objectives.

techniques.role: Defines the understanding horizon as the least fixed point of prerequisite expansion.
Provides constructive witnesses that closure membership follows from finitely many rule applications.
Connects one-concept reachable knowledge states to accessible union-closed learning spaces and proves a converse.
Turns prerequisite failure into an explicit learner-state-dependent erasure channel.
Tracks exact target uncertainty from the parsed public history.
Equates expected entropy decrease with one-round usable target information and telescopes it to identification.
Shows that expanding acquired knowledge creates a uniformly more informative parsed experiment.
Measures the minimum number of prerequisite-respecting acquisitions required to include a target.
Expresses optimal completion probability as a function of available teaching rounds.
Converts a deterministic acquisition step function into a concentrated-budget output example.
Constructs heterogeneous minds for which common instruction cannot reuse personalized prerequisite work.

evaluations.setting: Finite prerequisite-rule systems and their one-concept-at-a-time reachable acquired sets
evaluations.metric: Exact satisfaction of accessibility and union-closure axioms, plus converse representability
evaluations.result: Theorem 2.27 proves equivalence with an axiom-based learning space under the stated finite-horizon assumptions
evaluations.baseline: No empirical or algorithmic baseline; comparison is to the formal learning-space axioms

evaluations.setting: Finite Bayesian target teaching through the sharp parser
evaluations.metric: Expected completion rounds, structural distance, posterior entropy, conditional mutual information, and maximum parsed capacity
evaluations.result: For Cmax>0, Theorem 4.11 lower-bounds expected time by max(E[L_m(Theta)], H(Theta)/Cmax), while Proposition 4.13 upper-bounds it by E[L_m(Theta)]+1 and proves H/Cmax <= 1; the allowed H=Cmax=0 edge case makes the printed ratio undefined
evaluations.baseline: No competing teaching policy or simulation; Cmax is the log-cardinality of the sharp parser's output range and the lower bound is compared only with a constructive curriculum and one four-target toy example

evaluations.setting: Fixed-horizon acquisition for a deterministic target g with prerequisite depth L_m(g)
evaluations.metric: Optimal probability of target acquisition by t rounds
evaluations.result: The value is exactly 0 for t<L_m(g) and 1 for t>=L_m(g); random targets do not share this exact step in general
evaluations.baseline: No smooth-learning, random-curriculum, or human-capital baseline is evaluated; smooth production is only discussed conceptually

evaluations.setting: N identical deterministic-target learners sharing B instructional rounds
evaluations.metric: Number of learners that fully acquire the target
evaluations.result: Giving everyone fewer than L rounds completes zero, whereas concentrating L rounds completes min(N,floor(B/L))
evaluations.baseline: Uniform spreading is the sole stylized comparator; partial learning, fairness, and heterogeneous learner policies are absent

evaluations.setting: Constructed class of k minds, each with a private prerequisite chain of personalized length L
evaluations.metric: Shortest signal-sequence length reaching a common target in every mind
evaluations.result: Personalized curricula have length L, while the optimal common broadcast has exact length k(L-1)+1
evaluations.baseline: Personalization versus one open-loop broadcast on an adversarial construction; no average-case, feedback, grouping, or empirical classroom baseline

limitations: Author-stated: the framework deliberately omits analogy, abstraction, forgetting, semantic interpretation, and many other features of cognition.
Author-stated: it does not encode truth, logical inconsistency, belief revision, or semantic relations beyond prerequisite reachability.
Author-stated: the rule architecture is fixed; developmental change is represented by replacing the entire mind rather than learning the architecture.
Author-stated: the parser is memoryless and does not buffer an unparseable signal for later decoding, which could weaken lower bounds in a richer model.
Reviewer-identified: direct target signals force the headline epistemic lower bound to at most one round, leaving little demonstrated separation between structural and epistemic bottlenecks.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem 4.11 and Proposition 4.13 omit C_m^max>0 or a zero-capacity convention, so their ratio is undefined for an allowed deterministic target with a one-symbol signal system.

Reviewer-identified: the defined parsed 'capacity' is exactly log output-range cardinality under an optimized raw-input distribution, rather than a target-conditioned Shannon capacity with signaling constraints.
Reviewer-identified: the null observation can update the posterior, so describing every unparseable signal as indistinguishable noise is only eventwise, not generally distributional.

Reviewer-identified: exact Bayesian updating, full common knowledge, target-aware teaching, and knowledge of prerequisites make the teacher and learner substantially more informed than realistic educational agents.

Reviewer-identified: acquisition is irreversible, noiseless, atomic, and limited to one concept per round; practice, errors, spontaneous inference, transfer, parallelism, and varying concept cost are excluded.
Reviewer-identified: the deterministic target is required for the exact zero-to-one threshold and budget-concentration proposition; a random target may create several gradual steps.

Reviewer-identified: counting only completed learners mechanically favors concentration and cannot support welfare, fairness, or workforce policy without valuing partial mastery and downstream consequences.
Reviewer-identified: the linear broadcast penalty is existential and engineered through disjoint private chains, not a bound for arbitrary heterogeneous learners.
Reviewer-identified: a universal curriculum is modeled as an open-loop common sequence; classroom feedback, branching, peer learning, grouping, and shared prerequisites could sharply reduce the gap.
Reviewer-identified: no procedure infers C, A_m, or E_m from observations, so the model's central objects are assumed rather than estimated.
Reviewer-identified: no experiment tests descriptive validity, predictive calibration, or the empirical magnitude of any claimed threshold or broadcast penalty.
failure_modes: A learner stores an initially opaque explanation and understands it after later prerequisites, invalidating memoryless erasure-based timing claims.
One example teaches several concepts simultaneously or one nominal concept requires repeated practice, breaking the one-concept-one-round structural distance.
Prerequisites are probabilistic, context dependent, cyclic, or substitutable rather than deterministic finite conjunctions.
Observing bottom reveals the target class, so apparent erasure transmits more information than the informal noise metaphor suggests.
Distinct target signals are unavailable or ambiguous, making exact identification slower than the Proposition 4.13 baseline.
A deterministic single-target interface has zero entropy and zero parsed-output capacity, making the paper's ratio-form speed law undefined unless the zero case is separated.
The teacher mis-specifies a learner's rule system and emits an ordered sequence for the wrong mind, causing persistent non-acquisition.
Forgetting or interference removes prerequisites during a curriculum, so the monotone reachable-family analysis no longer applies.
Random target depths smooth the aggregate value curve, eliminating the single threshold used to motivate concentrated allocation.
Partial competence has high value or concentration has equity costs, reversing the allocation conclusion despite the completion count.
Learner types share prerequisite modules, permitting a broadcast curriculum to reuse work and making the private-chain linear penalty unrepresentative.
Adaptive feedback or grouping dominates both per-person personalization and a single open-loop broadcast, outside the stated comparison.
A fixed formal prerequisite graph fits observed sequences but has no semantic or causal relation to genuine understanding.
reusable_insights: Separate what is derivable in principle, what has actually been acquired, and what is currently one step parseable; conflating these states hides curriculum constraints.
Represent prerequisite-respecting knowledge states as a learning space or antimatroid when accessibility and union closure are empirically defensible.
Treat communication quality as learner-state dependent and report both the raw signal and the parsed observation when diagnosing instruction failure.
Distinguish eventwise erasure from statistical informativeness: even a common null token can encode which alternatives were impossible to parse.
Use Blackwell dominance, not only entropy, when claiming one learner state is more informative for every downstream decision problem.
Pair structural shortest-path bounds with a constructive curriculum; otherwise depth can be a pessimistic certificate with no attainable strategy.
Audit whether modeling conveniences trivialize one term of a multi-bottleneck theorem, as direct signaling does to the epistemic term here.
State information-budget results first as H(Theta)<=Cmax E[tau]; divide by Cmax only after proving it is positive and handle a zero-capacity deterministic case separately.
State deterministic and random-target threshold claims separately; only the former yields a single exact step without further assumptions.
Before recommending concentrated training, declare the outcome functional, partial-credit curve, fairness constraints, and learner heterogeneity.
Quantify prerequisite overlap across learners before choosing personalization, clustering, or broadcast; the disjointness pattern determines reuse.
Add a buffer state for previously unparseable signals as a decisive extension and compare completion times with the sharp memoryless parser.
open_questions: Can prerequisite rules and axiom sets be identified consistently from noisy learner trajectories rather than specified by a modeler?
Which empirical tests distinguish a true learning-space structure from a convenient union-closed approximation?
How do completion bounds change when unparseable signals are stored and reprocessed after prerequisites arrive?
What replaces the one-round epistemic term when target signals overlap, channels are noisy, or exact target-specific messages are unavailable?
How should the speed law be stated for zero parsed capacity, and which restrictions on target-dependent coding make its capacity term operational rather than output-cardinality bookkeeping?
Can concepts be acquired in bundles with variable duration while preserving a useful structural distance or submodular curriculum objective?
How should forgetting, misconception, contradiction, and belief revision be integrated without losing tractable reachability results?
For random targets, what conditions create a genuinely non-concave aggregate completion curve rather than a mixture of shallow and deep tasks?
Does concentrated instruction remain optimal under partial-credit utilities, risk aversion, fairness constraints, and downstream complementarity among learners?
What approximation guarantees are possible for adaptive group curricula when learner prerequisite graphs partially overlap?
Can teacher uncertainty over the mind be handled with robust or Bayesian curriculum design, and how expensive is active diagnosis?
Do real human or machine learners exhibit the predicted Blackwell monotonicity as prerequisites accumulate?
Which observable outcomes would falsify the claim that a particular failure is structural rather than motivational, semantic, or noisy?

competitive_landscape.title: Knowledge Spaces and Learning Spaces
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational direct predecessor for accessible, union-closed knowledge-state families and adaptive learning systems.
competitive_landscape.difference: It already develops the combinatorial learning-space framework, Markovian assessment processes, compact representations, and ALEKS deployments; the present paper derives a learning space from finitary prerequisite rules and adds a target-aware gated communication model, but offers no empirical assessment system.

competitive_landscape.title: Iterative Classroom Teaching
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strong direct competitor for common instruction to diverse learners and personalized grouping.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies one example stream for learners with different initial states and rates, proves an O(min(d,N) log(1/epsilon)) teaching bound, treats noisy knowledge of learner dynamics, and evaluates homogeneous partitions. The present paper's exact k(L-1)+1 gap is sharper only for an adversarial private-chain construction and omits feedback, noise, and experiments.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:1811.03537v2; revised 2018-11-12 (v1 submitted 2018-11-08; current revision checked 2026-08-23)

competitive_landscape.title: Class Teaching for Inverse Reinforcement Learners
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct heterogeneous-class teaching antecedent for deciding whether one demonstration can teach everyone.
competitive_landscape.difference: It formalizes and evaluates shared demonstrations for heterogeneous inverse-RL agents and reports conditions under which a single demonstration is impossible. The present work uses prerequisite parsing rather than reward inference and gives a closed-form constructed broadcast penalty, without algorithmic evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine Teaching of Active Sequential Learners
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct sequential and Bayesian-intent teaching predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: It nests an active learner inside an MDP, allows a planning teacher to answer learner-selected queries, and tests bandits in simulation and a user study. The present model makes the teacher the signal chooser and focuses on prerequisite-gated decoding, yielding structural theorems but no strategic-query or behavioral evidence.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:1809.02869v3; revised 2019-11-01 (v1 submitted 2018-09-08; current revision checked 2026-08-23)

competitive_landscape.title: Teaching to Learn: Sequential Teaching of Agents with Inner States
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct counterpoint to the fixed-mind assumption in sequential teaching.
competitive_landscape.difference: It explicitly models learners whose algorithm or latent inner state changes, optimizes future generalization through optimal control, and separates manipulative teaching from education. The present paper fixes prerequisite architecture and optimizes target completion, so it cannot represent teaching that improves how the learner learns.

competitive_landscape.title: An Optimal Control Approach to Sequential Machine Teaching
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct shortest-sequence predecessor for sequential machine teaching.
competitive_landscape.difference: It formulates minimum-length teaching as time-optimal control, derives Pontryagin conditions, and computes sequences that beat heuristics for least-squares gradient learners. The present paper replaces continuous learner dynamics with prerequisite reachability and obtains exact structural lengths, but does not solve general curriculum optimization.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 89, pages 2495-2503; published 2019-04-11 for AISTATS held 2019-04-16 through 2019-04-18 (official proceedings record checked 2026-08-23)

competitive_landscape.title: Iterative Machine Teaching
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor for state-aware sequential example selection and teaching complexity.
competitive_landscape.difference: It designs teachers with different visibility into an iterative learner, proves faster convergence, and validates on synthetic distributions and real images. The present paper's teacher acts through a parser-gated concept system and studies reachability thresholds rather than model-parameter convergence.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 70, pages 2149-2158; published 2017-07-17 for ICML held 2017-08-06 through 2017-08-11 (official proceedings record checked 2026-08-23)

competitive_landscape.title: Teaching with Limited Information on the Learner's Behaviour
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct realistic-information competitor to the omniscient-teacher baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies black-box learners whose algorithm and hypothesis class are unknown, allows unattainable targets and approximate teaching, gives bounds for smoother or randomized responses, and evaluates real data. The present theory assumes the prerequisite architecture and target are known to the teacher, enabling cleaner structural bounds at much stronger information assumptions.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 119, pages 2016-2026; published 2020-11-21 for ICML held 2020-07-13 through 2020-07-18 (official proceedings record checked 2026-08-23)

competitive_landscape.title: Representational Alignment Supports Effective Teaching
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current empirical competitor for the paper's claim that learner-relative representations govern teaching effectiveness.
competitive_landscape.difference: GRADE supplies controlled machine-machine and machine-human experiments showing that alignment improves learning but interacts with class size and representational diversity, then uses this for teacher matching. The present paper makes learner relativity exact through prerequisite rules but does not measure representations or outcomes in people or models.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 273, pages 146-173; workshop held 2025-03-03 and proceedings published 2025-03-31 (official proceedings record checked 2026-08-23)

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a mathematical theory in which prerequisite-relative parsing jointly produces structural and epistemic speed limits, non-concave finite-horizon returns, a case for concentrated training resources, and a linear personalization advantage across heterogeneous minds.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It proves closure and learning-space representation results, entropy and Blackwell statements for a sharp state-dependent parser, completion-time bounds, a deterministic threshold and allocation proposition, and an exact private-chain broadcast construction, with full proofs in the appendix.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The most credible novelty is the unusually unified chain from a prerequisite-rule closure system to a state-dependent communication channel and then to economic-style threshold and broadcast consequences. Learning spaces, sequential machine teaching, target-aware optimal control, black-box teaching, and heterogeneous classroom teaching are substantial predecessors that narrow the novelty. Moreover, the capacity reduces to parser-output cardinality, direct signaling collapses the epistemic term, its ratio needs a missing positive-capacity condition, the exact threshold is deterministic, and the broadcast penalty is existential. The work is a clean formal synthesis rather than an empirically established general theory of understanding.

verification.passage_check: Independently re-read the exact SHA-pinned 51-page arXiv:2603.19349v1 PDF and page-marked extraction end to end: main text pages 1-34, every closure/derivation/learning-space/information/threshold/broadcast proof on pages 35-48, all additional results on page 49, and references on pages 50-51. Traced every theorem hypothesis into its appendix proof, visually rechecked the speed-law statements and proofs on pages 28-30 and 44-46, and corrected misassigned anchors. The second pass confirmed the core finite representation and private-chain results but identified that C_m(K) is exactly log parser-output cardinality and that the permitted deterministic one-signal case makes H(Theta)/C_m^max equal 0/0 unless a positivity convention is added.
verification.competitor_check: Re-searched official primary literature and opened full official abstracts/records on 2026-08-23. Exact arXiv revisions checked were 1511.06757v1, 1811.03537v2, 1911.13009v1, 1809.02869v3, and 2009.06227v1; official proceedings versions checked were PMLR v89/lessard19a, v70/liu17b, v119/cicalese20a, and v273/sucholutsky25a. Titles, dates, mechanisms, learner-information assumptions, formal bounds, empirical settings, and direct relationships to learning spaces, sequential teaching, heterogeneous classrooms, black-box learners, and representational alignment were independently verified; the target was separately resolved as arXiv:2603.19349v1 and was not counted.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification covered every one of the 51 pinned pages and every appendix proof rather than relying on the primary record. The core results are sound under their stated finite, memoryless, one-concept-per-round model, apart from the concrete zero-denominator boundary defect; their cognitive and policy interpretations remain much broader than the formal constructions. Hashes and page coverage match the full-text index exactly. Nine current official primary competitor records were checked at exact arXiv or proceedings versions on 2026-08-23; the strongest novelty-narrowing omissions remain Iterative Classroom Teaching, Class Teaching for Inverse Reinforcement Learners, and empirical GRADE. Confidence is reduced slightly because no experiment makes the formal prerequisite graph or sharp parser empirically identifiable.
